title: I Used the Fly-Tying Vise Hours on the Mentor Who Left My Hook in the Jaws

parts.text: I sat at vise six at 7:05 p.m. and mentor Pike was already wrapping my numbered hook. The card said: ONE VISE. NINETY MINUTES. HOOK STAYS WITH THE BOOKING. I was forty, club member, holding a pattern card that listed our fly. Pike shrugged. "Mentors are the jaws." I photographed the card, the booking, and his bobbin on my thread. Then I asked for the vise log. At 7:13 the bench pinged why Pike's name was on my hook. I kept my voice bench-quiet and let the timestamp talk. A card is only a card until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The bench can see Pike's bobbin on my thread during our booking.

social.video_title: He wrapped my numbered hook in my jaws — Part 1/2
social.description: Fly-tying vise, a mentor on my thread, a ninety-minute card he posted. I logged the bobbin. Would you have asked for the vise log?

parts.text: Pike called it a demo until the bench asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the card, and the bobbin still. The hook went back to my foam. Pike ran his own ninety and told the next mentor atmosphere was always about hackle. Hackle is a word mentors use when a booking exists. Vise policy now has a second line: MENTORS ARE NOT THE JAWS. I keep our pattern on a labeled clip. Pike brown-bags his jokes. The bench finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Mentors are not the jaws — Part 2/2
social.description: Vise log, numbered hook, and a second line on the card. Was a demo ever my thread?
